doc: Q306 item 12: data/anatomy/muscle_groups_q306.json -- NEW groups with cited membership. The 19 groups a clinician names that this project had no membership data for at all (measured in docs/research/Q306_search_coverage_audit.md). Membership is taken from the references this project already cites, on the same basis Q283 used for its 17 named groups ("membership as in the cited source"). Three rules, applied without exception: * a member is listed only if the cited source places it in the group AND it resolves on at least one page; a member that resolves nowhere is recorded in `not_on_any_page` instead of being dropped silently, so the gap stays visible; * where the literature does not agree on the membership -- which is normal for the fascial compartments and for every "stabiliser" group -- the row carries contested=1 and says what varies, instead of picking a side silently; * nothing is inferred. A group whose membership this project cannot cite is not shipped at all.

sources.gray: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell), Elsevier 2019.
sources.moore: Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed., Wolters Kluwer 2018.
sources.karagiannakis2017: Karagiannakis D, Athanasopoulos S, Mandalidis D. Scapular muscles' activity in female volleyball players with scapular asymmetry in the resting position. J Bodyw Mov Ther 2017;22(3):580-585. doi:10.1016/j.jbmt.2017.09.018 (PMID 30100280) -- studies "the EMG activity of periscapular muscles (SA, UT and MT)", i.e. serratus anterior and the upper and middle trapezius, which is the set the clinical term 'scapular stabilisers' is normally used for.

he_note: HEBREW IS A PROJECT-SUPPLIED TRANSLATION, NOT A PUBLISHED TERMINOLOGY -- the same declaration data/anatomy/synonyms_q298.json carries in sources.he.

groups.name: Pelvic floor (pelvic diaphragm)
groups.note: Gray's names the pelvic diaphragm as levator ani plus coccygeus; obturator internus and piriformis form the pelvic WALLS, not the floor, and are listed because they bound the same space and the pages ship them -- the card says which is floor and which is wall. The pages ship levator ani as one mesh whose own name lists its parts ('Levator ani (pubococcygeus, puborectalis, iliococcygeus)'), so the parts are reachable through it rather than as separate members.

groups.name: Levator ani
groups.note: Gray's gives levator ani three parts: pubococcygeus, puborectalis and iliococcygeus. Members that resolve nowhere are recorded rather than dropped: on these pages levator ani ships as ONE mesh whose page name itself lists the three parts.

groups.name: Scapular (scapulothoracic) stabilisers
groups.contested_why: There is no textbook list called 'scapular stabilisers': the term is clinical. Gray's names the muscles that attach the scapula to the thorax (trapezius, the rhomboids, levator scapulae, serratus anterior, pectoralis minor, subclavius); the EMG literature usually means a narrower set -- Karagiannakis 2017 studies "periscapular muscles (SA, UT and MT)", serratus anterior and the upper and middle trapezius. Both are stated; neither is presented as the definition.

groups.name: Muscles of mastication
groups.note: The four muscles Gray's and Terminologia both name, all supplied by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve.

groups.name: Muscles of facial expression
groups.note: The muscles Gray's places in the face and supplied by the facial nerve. Only those that resolve on a page are listed as members; the rest are recorded in not_on_any_page.

groups.name: Muscles of inspiration
groups.contested_why: Gray's separates the PRIMARY muscles of inspiration (the diaphragm and the external intercostals) from the ACCESSORY ones recruited in forced or laboured breathing (the scalenes, sternocleidomastoid, serratus anterior, pectoralis minor, serratus posterior superior, levatores costarum). Which accessory muscles count varies by author, so both tiers are named and the card says which is which rather than merging them.

groups.name: Muscles of expiration
groups.note: Quiet expiration is passive; Gray's names these as the muscles of FORCED expiration, which the card states.

groups.name: Intrinsic muscles of the hand
groups.note: The muscles whose origin AND insertion are both within the hand. The thenar and hypothenar groups of data/anatomy/muscle_groups_q283.json are subsets of this group.

groups.name: Intrinsic muscles of the foot
groups.note: The muscles whose origin AND insertion are both within the foot.

groups.name: Anterior (flexor) compartment of the forearm
groups.note: A fascial compartment. The MEMBERSHIP is Gray's; the BOUNDARIES are where the literature disagrees, so no boundary claim is made here -- the group lists the muscles the cited source places in the compartment and the card names the fascia the pages actually ship.
groups.contested_why: Gray's divides this compartment into a superficial and a deep layer; some authors also describe an intermediate layer holding flexor digitorum superficialis alone. Both readings are named.

groups.name: Posterior (extensor) compartment of the forearm
groups.note: A fascial compartment. The MEMBERSHIP is Gray's; the BOUNDARIES are where the literature disagrees, so no boundary claim is made here -- the group lists the muscles the cited source places in the compartment and the card names the fascia the pages actually ship.
groups.contested_why: Gray's places brachioradialis and the two radial extensors in the posterior compartment although they flex or extend the wrist from the lateral side; other authors call them a separate 'mobile wad'. Both readings are named.

groups.name: Anterior compartment of the thigh
groups.note: A fascial compartment. The MEMBERSHIP is Gray's; the BOUNDARIES are where the literature disagrees, so no boundary claim is made here -- the group lists the muscles the cited source places in the compartment and the card names the fascia the pages actually ship.
groups.contested_why: Pectineus is placed in the ANTERIOR compartment by its nerve supply (femoral) and in the MEDIAL compartment by its action and position; Gray's notes both. It is therefore listed in both groups here, with this note, rather than assigned to one.

groups.name: Posterior compartment of the thigh
groups.note: A fascial compartment. The MEMBERSHIP is Gray's; the BOUNDARIES are where the literature disagrees, so no boundary claim is made here -- the group lists the muscles the cited source places in the compartment and the card names the fascia the pages actually ship.
groups.contested_why: Only the HAMSTRING part of adductor magnus belongs here; its adductor part is in the medial compartment. The pages ship adductor magnus as one mesh, so it appears in both groups and the card names the part, using the two compartments Q293 recorded for it.

groups.name: Medial compartment of the thigh
groups.note: A fascial compartment. The MEMBERSHIP is Gray's; the BOUNDARIES are where the literature disagrees, so no boundary claim is made here -- the group lists the muscles the cited source places in the compartment and the card names the fascia the pages actually ship. Identical membership to the named group `hip_adductors` of data/anatomy/muscle_groups_q283.json; this row exists so the COMPARTMENT name reaches it too.

groups.name: Superficial posterior compartment of the leg
syn: superficial posterior compartment of the leg
groups.note: A fascial compartment. The MEMBERSHIP is Gray's; the BOUNDARIES are where the literature disagrees, so no boundary claim is made here -- the group lists the muscles the cited source places in the compartment and the card names the fascia the pages actually ship.

groups.name: Deep posterior compartment of the leg
syn: deep posterior compartment of the leg
groups.note: A fascial compartment. The MEMBERSHIP is Gray's; the BOUNDARIES are where the literature disagrees, so no boundary claim is made here -- the group lists the muscles the cited source places in the compartment and the card names the fascia the pages actually ship.
groups.contested_why: Gray's places popliteus in the deep posterior compartment; some authors treat it as a separate knee muscle outside the compartments. Both readings are named.

groups.name: Transversospinalis group
groups.note: Gray's intermediate layer of the deep back: the semispinalis muscles, multifidus and the rotatores. The erector spinae group of data/anatomy/muscle_groups_q283.json is the layer superficial to it, not part of it.

groups.name: Lumbar multifidus
groups.note: A member of the transversospinalis group, listed separately because it is searched by name in lumbo-pelvic practice -- it is the muscle Jang & Jeon 2024 measured against pelvic tilt (see data/anatomy/concepts_q306.json, anterior_pelvic_tilt).
